reference.description: The verse he asks about: 'Romans 8:28', or a passage under a heading ('Romans 8:1-11').

greek.description: The Greek of the verse (the Byzantine text), in Greek word order.

english.description: The same verse in English (the Majority Standard Bible); words the translators supplied are between asterisks.

greek_words.description: Optional. The words of `greek`, in text order, each with its form as it stands in the text, its lemma (the dictionary form), the lexicon's gloss and its parsing in plain words, from the app's own chapter data, and the app's respelling, syllables and stress of the form; a word the text repeats with the same lemma and parsing is listed once. For a long passage the list may stop part-way.

respelling.description: The word as the app's pronunciation respells it, the stressed syllable in capitals.

syllables.description: The word cut into syllables by the app, in order, in Greek letters. Use these exactly for a question about how to say the word; never count or cut the word yourself.

stress.description: Only with syllables: the 0-based index of the stressed syllable in syllables (0 is the first). Absent when the word carries no accent.

hebrew.description: Optional. Only for a verse of the Old Testament, which has no Greek (`greek` is then an empty string): the verse in Biblical Hebrew (the Westminster Leningrad Codex), pointed, with the cantillation marks left off, written in reading order, the first word first. Aramaic words of the Old Testament are in it too.

hebrew_words.description: Optional. With `hebrew`: the words of `hebrew`, in text order, each with its form as it stands, its lemma (the TBESH headword), the table's transliteration, the lexicon's gloss and its parsing in plain words, from the app's own chapter data; a word the text repeats with the same lemma and parsing is listed once. A word has no `lemma`, `translit` or `gloss` when the data gives none. For a long passage the list may stop part-way.

question.description: What he asked, at most 4000 characters.

spoken.description: Optional. true only when he spoke the question to the phone's English speech recogniser (Hold to talk, Hold to ask); missing when he typed it. A Greek word in it may have come as English sound-alikes. See the instructions.

solid_count.description: Optional. How many Greek words he knows well in all. `solid_words` names only the most recent of them.

solid_words.description: The Greek lemmas he most recently came to know well: at most 50, the newest last. `solid_count` says how many he knows in all.

learner.description: Optional. Where he stands in one line: 'solid N words; learning: a, b, c; new today: x, y; due now: M'.

learner_grammar.description: Optional. Where his grammar stands, as in the Bible talk's request (grinds/bible-talk.input.schema.json learner_grammar).

memory.description: Optional. What Lampas remembers about him, which the app keeps on his phone (Settings > Memory) and chose for this ask: `index` is the short index of everything remembered (his own lines, then a list of the notes, one line each: the note's name and its first line), and `notes` are the notes the app picked by name for this place, word or screen (`book:<Book>` for the book of the reference, `word:<lemma>` for the word he asked about, `topic:<screen>` for the screen he is on), each `name` and `text`. At most three; read the index first, then the notes. Use it quietly as `learner_profile` is used: let it shape the answer, never repeat it back to him, and never let it change what is true about the text. Missing when nothing is kept.

index.description: The index as it is kept, at most 1500 characters; may be empty when only notes are named.

missing_foundations.description: Optional. Present only when the grammar words of his question name a topic that rests on ideas he has not learned (not yet, or not at all): `topic` is the idea he asked about, `total` how many ideas under it he lacks, and `ideas` the lowest on the ladder first (at most 8), so `ideas[0]` is his next step in the progression. `direct` marks an idea the topic itself names as a need: those are the most important. Offer a `bridge` from this list and never name an idea that is not in it (see the instructions, 'When he is not ready for the question').

topic.description: The title of the idea he asked about: 'The genitive case'.

total.description: How many ideas under the topic he lacks, all of them (the list names at most 8).

id.description: The idea's id, to put in `bridge`.

title.description: The idea's title, as he sees it: 'Pairs of vowels'.

direct.description: true when the topic itself names this idea as a need.

learner_profile.description: Optional. Who he is as a student, which he kept himself in Settings > About you; every field is optional and a field he has not filled in is missing (the whole field is missing when he has filled in none). age: a number or a band, as he wrote it. pace: how fast he wants to go. ways: how he learns best (hearing, seeing, reading, doing = hands-on). background: languages he knows, Greek or Bible before, in his words. why: why he is learning Greek, in his words. notes: short things the tutor has learned about him, the newest last. Meet him where he is; never repeat this back to him. learned, observed_pace, observed_ways and do_not_ask are what the app itself found out; see them as hints at the same fields, weaker than what he wrote.

learned.description: What the tutor itself learned about him in earlier talks, for a field he did not fill in himself: field, value, and guessed true when it is only a guess from how he writes and talks (never state a guess as a fact, and let anything he told you or chose win over it).

observed_pace.description: How he seems to go, which the phone worked out from how fast and how rightly he answers in reviews, quizzes and drills: quick, steady or slow. Missing until he has answered enough. It may differ from the `pace` he chose; his choice wins.

observed_ways.description: What he uses, as whole percents the phone counted: hearing (verses and words said aloud), seeing (pictures he sent), reading (chapters and verses read) and doing (quiz, review and drill answers, readings aloud). A way with no use is left out; missing until he has used the app enough. A hint at how he likes to learn, not a fact.

do_not_ask.description: The profile fields you must not ask him about in this talk: asked in the last day, or he declined to say. Missing when none.

rusty.description: Optional. The solid words and grammar ideas he now slips on (a wrong answer among his last three) or has not met for a long while (a week or more past due), worst first, at most 8. Each: `kind` 'word' or 'idea', `id` (the word's dictionary form, or the idea's id), `title` (what to call it) and `why` (the plain reason, such as 'slipped twice this week' or 'not seen for 3 weeks'). Missing when nothing is rusty, and in a quiz. It is the app's own list, worked out from his answers: never add an item to it or name one that is not in it (see the instructions, 'When he has gone rusty').

works.description: Optional. A digest of his Logos shelf chosen by the place he is on, never the whole shelf: first the books he pinned, then the commentaries whose volume covers this chapter (at most 8), then, for a question about a form or a reading, his grammars (at most 4) and Greek texts (at most 3), then any book that takes a `place`; no lexicon. This verse answer links nothing: the digest tells you what he keeps, so you may say that a commentary of his covers this chapter, or that his other books are under In another book on the verse. Each line is `id` (the value of a `work` link, exactly as given), `t` (a short title), `k` (what it is: c commentary, g grammar, t Greek text or apparatus, i interlinear, b book) and `p` (1 for a book that takes a `place` of its own: write it book.chapter, such as 3.24, or book.chapter.section, such as 3.21.5, the Institutes' four books having 18, 17, 25 and 20 chapters; name a place only when you know the chapter treats the question). The last line, `more`, counts the books of his shelf that are not listed, by kind: say 'your other commentaries are under In another book' and never that he has none. Missing when he has nothing of these on his shelf.

id.description: The work's key, the value of a `work` link.

k.description: c commentary, g grammar, t Greek text or apparatus, i interlinear, b book.

p.description: 1 for a book that takes a `place` of its own (the Institutes).

more.description: How many books of each kind (commentary, grammar, greek-text, interlinear, book) are on his shelf and not listed.

requests.description: Optional. The requests he has sent to the factory (an ask the tutor offered to pass on, an approach he asked for), at most the 10 newest, newest first, each with where it stands. Missing when he has sent none. status: sent (the factory has it, nothing more yet), filed (the makers have it on their list), building (being built now), landed (built and shipped; `version` is the app version it is in), declined (the makers decided not to; `reason` is why) or adopted-as-setting (it became a setting; `setting` is where Settings has it). Answer 'what happened to my idea' from this, never from a guess.

summary.description: What he asked for, in one line.

version.description: Only with landed: the app version the idea shipped in.

setting.description: Only with adopted-as-setting: the setting's name, as the makers wrote it ('Settings > Appearance > Sepia').

reason.description: Only with declined: why, in one plain sentence.

pronunciation.description: Optional. The Greek pronunciation the app speaks and respells in, by its id. Its rules are in pronunciation_guide.

pronunciation_guide.description: Optional. The name of that pronunciation and the sound rules the app speaks and respells by, from its pronunciation scheme. Describe a Greek sound by these rules.

hebrew_pronunciation_guide.description: Optional. The same for Hebrew: the name of the Hebrew pronunciation (settings.hebrewPronunciation) and the sound rules the app speaks and respells by. Describe a Hebrew sound by these rules. Missing for a reader who has no Hebrew.

facts.description: Optional. What the app read for you before this turn, by name (the app's tutor client, mw-t3xu9a.4): `where-he-is` (the screen he is on, `route`, in the Reader its book, chapter, view and verse, the sheets open), `today-drill` (his drill for today) and `settings` (the same as the field `settings`). Read-only copies of what the app holds now; use them as you use the fields they repeat. A fact the app dropped for room is still in `catalogue`.

catalogue.description: Optional. Every fact and place the app has, sorted by `name`: `is` (fact or place), `core` (true for a fact always sent) and `tell`, what it is (cut when the request is too big). Today it only names what the app has; nothing here is asked for or opened by your answer yet.

hebrew_interest.description: Optional. The Hebrew dial as he set it (Settings > How much Hebrew?), from 0, Just English, to 5, All in: `level`, its `name` and `next`, the one step above it. Present with `settings`, whose `greekInterest` is the Greek dial. The language of the verse's chapter picks the dial that matters to the answer: `hebrew_interest` for an Old Testament verse, `greekInterest` for a New Testament one.

settings.description: Optional. The app settings that bear on an answer, by key: hebrewDepth (how a Hebrew word is written), askBy ("speaking" or "typing"), englishAccent ("american", "british" or "ipa": the English the reader hears sounds in), readTutor (whether answers are read aloud to him), weave and weaveGrammar (how much Greek is woven into his English), greekInterest and hebrewInterest ("0" Just English to "5" All in: how much Greek, and how much Hebrew, he has asked the app to show): { "hebrewDepth": "both", "askBy": "speaking" }.
